title: Henderson shines as Chelsea bounce back by thrashing Bournemouth
description: Chelsea responded emphatically to their pre-international break defeat at Brentford with a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.Jordan Henderson scored twice, including a stunning free-kick...
fullText:
Chelsea responded emphatically to their pre-international break defeat at Brentford with a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

Jordan Henderson scored twice, including a stunning free-kick, as Xabi Alonso's side climbed to fifth in the early Premier League table.

Chelsea made a flying start, taking the lead after just 65 seconds when Henderson curled in off the post following good work from Cole Palmer.

Morgan Rogers doubled the advantage less than a minute later, with his effort deflecting off Antonio Silva and into the far corner as Chelsea went 2-0 up inside two-and-a-half minutes.

Bournemouth threatened before half-time when Rayan was denied by Emi Martinez, but Chelsea struck again just 30 seconds after the restart. Silva's error allowed Pedro Neto to set up Joao Pedro, who fired home.

Evanilson pulled one back following a scramble from a set-piece, but Chelsea quickly restored control.

Joao Pedro grabbed his second from Pep Chavarria's cross before Henderson completed the scoring with a superb free-kick to seal an emphatic victory.

title: Guimaraes puts Arsenal's title defence back on track, Chelsea shine
description: Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit. After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.
fullText:
Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.

After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.

However, Riccardo Calafiori drew the champions level when he converted Ben White's header from close range in the 62nd minute, before substitute Bruno Guimaraes struck the decisive blow just six minutes after he came off the bench.

Arteta said of Guimaraes: "This is the level for Arsenal, every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at.

"Against Brighton he wasn't at that level, and today he was much better, and he can still be much better, and that's what we have to demand."

Arsenal were below their best against a well-drilled Leeds side, who, prior to the contest, were unbeaten in the league.

But the Gunners' revival here puts their championship defence back on course, and places the onus on City, with Enzo Maresca's side contesting their first match since the club were found guilty of an avalanche of financial breaches, at Liverpool on Sunday.

Jordan Henderson was the unlikely hero as Chelsea's entertainers blew Bournemouth away in a comprehensive and chaotic 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

Former Liverpool captain Henderson, 36, scored two and set up one for Morgan Rogers while Joao Pedro also hit the net twice for the rampant Blues.

Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea extended Alvaro Arbeloa's winless start to six Premier League matches.

Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were both on the scoresheet as 10-man Brighton clinched a 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Kristoffer Ajer's second-half equalizer ensured Brentford continued their unbeaten start to the Premier League season in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.

title: Loud blast at Riyadh airport as travelers evacuated and airlines cancel flights
description:
Many people were wounded in a blast at Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, according ‌to two eyewitnesses and two people briefed on the matter, and travellers ‌were evacuated from parts of the facility. 
   One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then ​seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport. 
   The Saudi government's media office and the Saudi civil aviation authority did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the ‌incident. 
   Saturday's incident comes amid an ⁠escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on the kingdom.
fullText:
RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Many people were wounded in a blast at Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, according ‌to two eyewitnesses and two people briefed on the matter, and travellers ‌were evacuated from parts of the facility.

One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then ​seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport.

The Saudi government's media office and the Saudi civil aviation authority did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the ‌incident.

Saturday's incident comes amid an ⁠escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this week, leaving ⁠four people dead and others wounded, and badly damaging an aircraft.

Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter ​hovering over ​the airport at one point.

The airport urged ​passengers to contact their airlines ‌directly and check their flight status before heading there.

Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there.

Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations ‌extending into Monday.

Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier ​in the week had already prompted a number ​of carriers to suspend or ​cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is ‌due to host major energy and investment ​conferences.

Organisers of those ​conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.

The Houthis have said airliners should avoid ​Saudi airspace, declaring it ‌a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an ​offensive against the group earlier this month.

title: A €30m steal, Liverpool have green light to sign elite talent
description: Liverpool have got the chance to snap up one of the world's most exciting young talents. A €30m steal, no less.Liverpool are on a mission to find elite young talent. Some have been locked down alrea...
fullText:
Liverpool have got the chance to snap up one of the world's most exciting young talents. A €30m steal, no less.

Liverpool are on a mission to find elite young talent. Some have been locked down already, with the likes of Jeremy Jacquet thriving in the first-team team right and looking set for a long, exciting future.

Then there are others who have agreed to join down the line. Liverpool struck two deals a year in advance this summer, and they're currently looking to find more.

It's quite clearly a major plan at Anfield right now. They want to build their next first-team - or at least the core of it - a long time in advance and that means paying fairly large sums on what are essentially gambles.

There's rightly a lot of hype around Gilberto Mora right now. The 17-year-old was the youngest player at the summer's World Cup and then he grabbed his first international goal during this break.

Mora is expected to leave Tijuana shortly. In fact, the only reason he's stuck around there is because he can't move before turning 18 but January represents a golden opportunity for him to depart.

Liverpool's long-standing interest will put them in a strong position to get him and it seems Tijuana are ready to sell. Journalist Cesar Luis Merlo reports on his YouTube channel that Mora can move for between €20m and €30m next year.

That may well be a steal. Mora is playing well beyond his years and does look like the kind of player who develops steadily and consistently - he's not dependent on pace, has strong technique, and is already capable of playing against elite professionals.

That green light at €30m looks like a fantastic deal, really. Liverpool are in the mix and have been for months - now's their opportunity to snap him up.

So keep an eye on this one. Mora may well arrive as one of the most exciting prospects in years.

title: Mbappe, Trent start in a 4-2-3-1: How Real Madrid can line up against Villarreal
description: Following a three-week hiatus due to the international break, Real Madrid are back in action later tonight as they host Villarreal in La Liga at the Santiago Bernabeu.The Spanish capital giants find t...
fullText:
Following a three-week hiatus due to the international break, Real Madrid are back in action later tonight as they host Villarreal in La Liga at the Santiago Bernabeu.

The Spanish capital giants find themselves under intense pressure, having succumbed to a defeat to Atletico Madrid in the derby right before the break.

The result has left Jose Mourinho & co. trailing arch-rivals FC Barcelona by six points, with the Catalans sitting comfortably at the top of the table, having won all of their matches so far.

Therefore, Real Madrid have no margin for error as they take on Villarreal, knowing that another slip-up could put further distance between themselves and Hansi Flick's men.

The good news for Mourinho is that he has recovered some of his injured stars as Kylian Mbappe and Ibrahima Konate are back to fitness after returning from international duty with minor injuries.

Furthermore, Federico Valverde, who suffered an injury in the derby, has also recovered and been included in the squad list to face the Yellow Submarine.

However, Eder Militao remains unavailable, along with Ferland Mendy, Raul Asencio, and Rodrygo Goes. Dean Huijsen also misses out through suspension.

Here's how Real Madrid could take the field at the Santiago Bernabeu against Villarreal.

Thibaut Courtois will man the goal as usual for Real Madrid and will be hoping to keep a clean sheet, having not managed a single one in their last five matches.

Fit to start. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, in defence, Ibrahima Konate is expected to start from the get-go despite only recently recovering from a knock, given the absences in defence. Partnering the summer signing will be veteran defender Antonio Rudiger.

There is intense competition at right-back, but Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to edge out Denzel Dumfries for the starting spot, considering that he had a lighter workload during the international break compared to the Dutchman.

On the opposite side, Alvaro Carreras is expected to get the nod ahead of summer signing Marc Cucurella, who was heavily involved with Spain during the international window.

Mourinho has yet to figure out his best midfield combination as Real Madrid look for ways to control and dictate matches.

While Fede Valverde has started each of Real Madrid's games so far, he is only returning from a considerably serious ankle injury and might not be risked from the start.

This should pave the way for veteran star Bernardo Silva to start in the centre of the park, from where he will hope to provide the team with creativity and vision.

Bernardo Silva to get a starting berth? (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images)

Partnering the Portuguese international will be Aurelien Tchouameni, who has worked hard during the international break to regain his peak fitness and rhythm.

Eduardo Camavinga, who impressed for France under Zinedine Zidane, will have minutes off the bench.

Jude Bellingham has been Real Madrid's best player so far this season and will line up as the attacking midfielder.

There has been a lot of talk surrounding Vinicius Jr and his poor form and the possibility that Mourinho could decide to bench the Brazilian. However, for now, the superstar winger is expected to start against Villarreal on the left flank.

On the right side of the attack, Arda Guler is expected to get the nod from the get-go, meaning marquee summer signing Yan Diomande will have to wait for his opportunity.

Kylian Mbappe, despite only recently recovering from an injury, will be leading the line for Real Madrid tonight at the Santiago Bernabeu.

title: 😮 Blackout after three minutes! Wagner off to a bad start at Hannover

fullText:
This certainly isn't how Sandro Wagner imagined the start of his second spell as a head coach. He arrived at Hannover 96 before the international break amid considerable optimism.

So far, the coach has had little to smile about on his debut in Magdeburg today. Quite the opposite: his team treated him to a major defensive lapse right from the start.

Although the visitors started on the front foot and pressed high, it was 1. FC Magdeburg who scored the first goal of the day. Hannover goalkeeper Leo Weinkauf took too long before passing to teammate Franz Roggow under pressure. Roggow also dallied, and his attempted clearance went wrong. Moritz Kwarteng caught him by surprise from behind, stuck out a foot and deflected the ball into the left corner of the net, leaving the keeper with no chance (3rd minute).

Sandro Wagner's time at the Lower Saxony club therefore begins with a slapstick goal and a very early deficit. There is still plenty of time, though, to turn this nightmare start around.

title: Erik Prince's private forces ambushed in Congo with former UFC fighter among wounded
description:
Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said.
The frontline clash ‌shows how Prince, an ally and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has taken on an expanded role in Congo through his company Vectus Global. The company, which ‌also operates in Haiti and other parts of Africa, provides consulting and security services and previously helped Congo's army secure the city of Uvira in South Kivu against Rwanda-backed rebels who control swathes of the east.
A veteran special operator reported on ​his podcast earlier this week that former US Green Beret and Ultimate Fighting Championship contestant Tim Kennedy was injured in Congo. The involvement of Prince's forces and the number of casualties have not previously been reported.
fullText:
DAKAR, Oct 9 (Reuters) - Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said.

The frontline clash ‌shows how Prince, an ally and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has taken on an expanded role in Congo through his company Vectus Global. The company, which ‌also operates in Haiti and other parts of Africa, provides consulting and security services and previously helped Congo's army secure the city of Uvira in South Kivu against Rwanda-backed rebels who control swathes of the east.

A veteran special operator reported on ​his podcast earlier this week that former US Green Beret and Ultimate Fighting Championship contestant Tim Kennedy was injured in Congo. The involvement of Prince's forces and the number of casualties have not previously been reported.

The attack in South Kivu on September 17 left about 20 dead and wounded, two sources working with Congo's government said. The dead included at least seven Congolese and a former member of New Zealand's Special Forces, while the wounded included Kennedy and another foreign contractor, the sources said.

A Vectus Global representative declined to comment. The company has not previously suffered casualties in Congo, a source with direct ‌knowledge of the operation said.

One of the sources who works for ⁠Congo's government said that Rwandan forces backing the M23 rebels may have surprised them by tracking a drone used for surveillance operations to their location.

Spokespeople for the Congolese and Rwandan governments and for the M23 did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Kennedy, the former mixed martial arts fighter, survived the attack ⁠with three gunshot wounds to the leg, three sources said, and is being treated at the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in the suburbs of Washington.

Kennedy has a popular podcast channel and millions of followers on social media. Trump is a fan of UFC, hosting fights at the White House this year.

The US State Department and Walter Reed declined to comment. Kennedy's parents did not respond to requests for comment.

A ​Congolese ​security source, who said some 20 people were wounded and killed in the attack, added that villagers were likely ​among the casualties as well. Reuters spoke to at least 10 sources ‌either with direct knowledge of the attack or briefed on the outcome.

PRINCE TOOK EXPANDED ROLE IN CONGO'S CONFLICT

Prince's initial mandate in Congo was to secure and improve revenue collection from the country's vast mineral reserves, which have been plundered for decades, fuelling relentless conflict in the east.

But in January and early February, his forces deployed to Uvira after Washington helped broker a deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from the strategic town.

The size of Prince's forces in Congo is unclear.

One of the sources with direct knowledge of the attack said the Vectus team was travelling between locations when the ambush took place and its sophistication suggested Rwandan forces were involved.

"It reinforces the need for DRC sovereignty to be restored. It's an incredibly dangerous place right now," the source said.

Two ‌other sources said the ambush was carried out by the Rwandan military.

Prince is the founder of now-defunct ​private military firm Blackwater, some of whose members were pardoned in 2020 for killing Iraqi civilians.

The State Department has ​said it does not have any contracts with Prince in Congo, though US officials have ​said they plan to work more closely with Vectus Global in Haiti.

The deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from Uvira was part of wider agreements brokered ‌by the Trump administration to try to end the conflict in eastern ​Congo.

Kennedy, a father of four, has posted ​his views on politics, culture, fitness and more on social media. He also runs a popular YouTube podcast in which he interviews UFC fighters, veterans, cultural disruptors and others.

He has often posted about his family, including four young children. In late August, he posted about having "incredible conversations about what being a man means and what sacrifice really looks like" ​with his son. He did not disclose details about his upcoming ‌trip to Congo.

The United Nations and Western powers say Rwanda backs M23, even exercising command and control over the group. Rwanda denies this. Fighting in the decades-long ​conflict flared early last year, with M23 fighters making rapid gains in the east, which is rich in tantalum, gold, lithium and other minerals.

(Additional reporting by Clement ​Bonnerot in Dakar and David Lewis in London; Writing by Jessica Donati; Editing by Aidan Lewis)

title: NI debut 'something I thought had passed' - Elmore
description: Northern Ireland's World Cup hopes may have all but come to an end against Portugal, but for Kess Elmore the 4-0 defeat marks the start of a long-awaited international journey.
fullText:
Northern Ireland's World Cup hopes may have all but come to an end against Portugal, but for Kess Elmore the 4-0 defeat marked the start of a long-awaited international journey.

After a ruthless first-half display from Portugal in Larne gave them a comfortable advantage at the break, Elmore's half-time introduction made an impact for Northern Ireland, who were much improved after the interval.

Elmore was a surprise call-up for the play-off double header against world number 22-ranked Portugal after having been involved in an NI training camp in 2021 and thought her chance to pull on a green shirt was over.

"I wasn't expecting Michael to call me. It was in the back of my mind, but definitely something that I kind of thought had passed," Elmore said.

"I've played in a lot of teams with a lot of different formations, tactics and, over the years, I have gained a real understanding of the game. So, hopefully I can bring a bit of that experience into the squad because we do have a young squad and I bring an attacking presence.

"It's great to have those experiences under my belt because now going into these games, I feel pretty confident in what I can do and what I can bring."

Elmore's debut came on a difficult evening for Northern Ireland, who struggled against a clinical Portugal side at Inver Park.

However, Elmore gave her side a different dimension to their attack with the debutant bringing energy and movement in the final third.

"I had no idea whether I'd make my debut or not, but I got told at half-time that I'd be coming on and, obviously, that was really nice to hear," she continued.

"I just wanted to come on and bring energy and work for the team. Portugal had a lot of momentum in the first half, so I kind of wanted to shift that in our favour and I feel like the second half was a lot better.

"So, I'm happy that I could contribute to that. We knew it was going to be a very defensive game for us but huge respect to Portugal and what they can do."

While the Northern Ireland fans will feel a lot of disappointment after the four-goal defeat, Elmore's performance offered an encouraging glimpse of what she could bring to the young squad.

She was also just one of three players who earned their first cap against Portugal, underlining McArdle's determination to wide his options and build depth within the squad.

Despite Elmore normally playing on either the wing or in midfield for Sparta Prague, she spent much of her time at Inver Park leading the NI line as a lone striker.

For a player who has already tested herself on some of European football's biggest club stages, including the Champions League and Europa League this year, Elmore added this was another challenge she would embrace.

"That was the first time playing centre-forward for a very long time since university.

"I like any of the attacking positions and anywhere attacking, I'm happy to play. I mean, anywhere the team needs me, I'm happy to be there."

Manager McArdle also believes the England youth international can add to the squad, who will now travel to Portimao on Tuesday (19:45 BST) but face a tough task.

"I think with Kess come on, obviously making her debut as well, I think that brings a nice energy," McArdle said.

"I'm grateful that we've all seen Kess because you'll see what I see now. There is someone here who can add to the group and give us something going forward and in the final third, so delighted that she's gone on the pitch."

title: Raphinha's brilliant Barcelona start interrupted by injury concerns
description: Raphinha will miss Barcelona's next two fixtures after returning from international break with an injury.
fullText:
Raphinha has made a phenomenal start to the season for Barcelona, cementing his status as one of Europe's most formidable attackers.

The 29-year-old has scored 14 times and provided three assists as the Spanish champions have racked up eight successive wins in all competitions.

His performances have been so impressive that his omission from the 30-man Ballon d'Or shortlist prompted debate, with some arguing his form warranted greater recognition among the game's elite.

Yet, just as Raphinha appeared ready to take his game to another level, injury concerns have interrupted his momentum and he looks set to miss Barcelona's next two fixtures.

Facing a demanding run of fixtures, including meetings with Paris St-Germain and Real Madrid this month in the Champions League and La Liga, keeping the Brazilian fit could prove just as important as making the most of his remarkable goalscoring form.

Raphinha withdrew from international duty with a right thigh injury after he was substituted at half-time in Brazil's match against Australia.

"The tests show something," Barcelona boss Hansi Flick told the media.

"It's not a serious injury, but we have to be careful because he had three injuries last year, and we have to take care of him."

Flick defended Raphinha's decision to want to play for Brazil.

"It's the national team and everyone wants to play for their national team," he said. "That's Raphinha's mentality. Always give 100%."

Although the setback does not appear to be major, the timing has not been ideal.

"We must reflect on whether it was necessary for him to play in Australia, travelling so many thousands of kilometres," added Flick. "It's incredible. They have to choose friendly matches and in Europe it is not possible because of the Nations League."

With tough tests to come, Flick will want all his leading attackers available and hope even a short spell on the sidelines won't disrupt Raphinha's rhythm.

The situation has also presented Flick with a familiar dilemma. At the start of the season, there were concerns Barcelona had no established number nine after veteran Poland striker Robert Lewandowski left the club.

Raphinha has mainly been playing as a false nine this season, rather than his usual role on the wing and the team have looked unstoppable.

They sit top of La Liga, five points clear of Atletico Madrid and Real Betis, with Real Madrid a point further back in fourth place, and thrashed Feyenoord 5-1 in their Champions League opener. With 36 goals scored and eight conceded, they've been dominant at both ends of the pitch.

For now, fellow Brazilian Gabriel Jesus - a deadline-day arrival from Arsenal in September - is likely to cover Raphinha's absence for the next two matches against Getafe on Saturday and then the European trip to Galatasaray.

Flick, though, has huge depth in his Barcelona squad, and Anthony Gordon, Dani Olmo and Karim Adeyemi could all play as a false nine if necessary.

Raphinha's numbers tell an impressive story, but his contribution to Barcelona extends beyond the stats.

He is the team captain and has become a central figure in their aggressive, high-intensity approach, combining direct attacking play with relentless pressing and a willingness to work for the team.

His finishing has become a defining feature of his game. Rather than relying on creating chances for others, Raphinha has developed into a consistent source of goals himself and Barcelona's performances so far have reflected that influence.

The former Leeds United player has been a key factor in why Flick's side have looked so threatening in the final third and could equal the 2013-14 record for the best start to a La Liga season if they beat Getafe for an eighth straight league win.

Raphinha, though, will be determined to avoid a repeat of last season, which demonstrated how quickly fitness problems can complicate the club's plans and ambition.

He was restricted to 33 appearances, with recurring fitness issues and a hamstring injury contributing to his absences.

Raphinha played seven times in the Champions League but, crucially, was missing as his side went out in the quarter-finals with defeat by Atletico Madrid.

His tally of 21 goals helped deliver the league title and he scored twice in a standout performance in the Spanish Super Cup final against Real Madrid.

Given his importance, the temptation for Flick to rush Raphinha back will be understandable and Barca will hope this is a brief interruption rather than the beginning of another frustrating injury cycle.

title: Crocker sets sights on route back to the top
description: Lewis Crocker is looking forward and not back at his world title defeat by Liam Paro as he prepares for his return against Owen Cooper in December at Belfast's 02.
fullText:
The flight home from Australia in June was a little longer for Lewis Crocker as he pondered his defeat by Liam Paro in his first defence of the IBF welterweight title.

A storming finish by the Belfast man was not enough to turn things around as all three judges gave Paro a 115-113 decision and the Australian realised his dream of becoming a two-weight champion.

Crocker grew into that fight and seemed on the brink of finding a finish in the late rounds, but Paro held on and Crocker lost his grip on the title he won last September in Belfast's Windsor Park against Paddy Donovan - his record slipping to 22 wins with one loss.

"Shoulda, woulda, coulda," is how the 29-year-old reflects on that night in Brisbane - one in which he was so near yet so far away, yet his first career defeat has not dented confidence, but only served to fuel his desire to rise again.

"I got beaten on a very close decision in a world title fight against a two-weight world champion," Crocker told BBC Sport NI.

"I gained experience from it anyway, and at 29 I've still got plenty more for whatever opportunity is coming.

"I felt like I had him hurt a lot of times and he was holding, if he gets a point taken off then I win the fight. Shoulda, woulda, coulda...

"That was a long fight back, but I'm over it because I know I'm right there. My main focus now is going to be a two-time world champion."

The first step on that quest takes place at The O2 in Belfast on 19 December when Crocker faces former English champion Owen Cooper [12-2] on the undercard of the Anthony Cacace v Nick Ball world super-featherweight title clash.

Perhaps it's further evidence that the old promotional cold war in British boxing is over as Crocker - promoted by Matchroom - will box on a Queensberry card and he is delighted to be back on home turf, promising fans a "Christmas Crocker" on the night.

That his first world title defence didn't take place in his home city instead of over 10,000 miles away on the east coast of Australia could be a source of consternation.

However, Crocker has always held a philosophical view of it all, insisting the opportunity to defend a world title in Australia is "something you'd dream of as a kid".

Still, it is good to be home as he embarks upon a route back to the top and while opportunities may present themselves in 2027, Crocker is not looking past the challenge of 26-year-old Cooper who will see this as his golden ticket.

"It would have been great to have a first defence in Belfast, but ultimately it doesn't matter - there's still two men getting into the ring," Crocker reasoned.

"It's good to be back in Belfast anyway, and get on the road to two-time world champion.

"More than anything now, I want to be a two-time world champion and we've a great plan ahead but I'm not looking past Owen, because he's a great fighter and I'm expecting a really tough test."

Crocker's old foe Paddy Donovan is front of the queue to face Paro, while the welterweight division has come alive once again with some of the sport's biggest names in Ryan Garcia [WBC], Teofimo Lopez [WBA] and Devin Haney [WBO] holding the other titles.

A second shot at a title at Windsor Park where he won his first against Donovan "would be great" but whomever and wherever, Crocker would be happy to take.

"There are four world titles out there, so any one of them [would be great]," he continued.

"[I plan to get] back on track and push towards it, but as I say, Owen's my main focus right now."

title: Wales must improve in World Cup bid - Wilkinson
description: Rhian Wilkinson accepts Wales must raise their standards after they scrape to a 1-0 victory in their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final in Albania.
fullText:
Rhian Wilkinson accepted Wales must raise their standards after they scraped to a 1-0 victory in their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final in Albania.

Wales have the upper hand going into Tuesday's second leg in Llanelli after Ezmiralda Franja's first-half own goal gave them victory in Shkoder.

But Wilkinson's team were fortunate to triumph against a team who sit 37 places below them in the Fifa rankings after Albania created the game's best chances.

"We stuck with it. [It was a] resilient performance. Not our best, but equally, we learned to win on hard days, and today it wasn't our best," the Wales head coach said.

"Coming home with [the win] is great. We're halfway there.

"We need to make sure we take care of business at home but equally push our standards a bit."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final second leg

Tuesday, 13 October at 19:15 BST

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Wilkinson had set a clean sheet as Wales' primary target in Albania and her players delivered on that score, albeit in fortuitous fashion.

While Wales' attacking threat was limited, Franja, Fortesa Berisha and Megi Doci all came close for the home side.

Albania's failure to convert one of their opportunities meant that just as had been the case in their three away games in the group stage of World Cup qualifying, Wales claimed a positive result despite being frustrated with aspects of their performance.

"I didn't think we defended overly well today to be honest, but what we did do is we never quit," Wilkinson added.

"I do think I've been in this job long enough to have seen that growth with this team, that we're finding ways to stick in the game.

"And we've got to be happy with that right now because, again, we're away from home and in an environment where they made it really tough."

Wales thumped Albania 4-0 in Wrexham on their way to winning Group B4, during which they thumped Montenegro in Llanelli and claimed a rousing 3-1 success against the Czech Republic in Cardiff.

They return to Parc y Scarlets hoping another dominant home performance will send them through to a two-legged play-off final in December.

Wales beat Albania in World Cup play-off first leg

"Albania will feel like they were right in this game and they were," Wilkinson said.

"So we've got to make sure that we match their energy and take advantage of the stretch in the game that they're going to give us because they're going to go for it.

"It's another battle. I'm confident in my team, but we've got to be ready to fight because definitely Albania will be."

Should they progress, Wales look likely to face Norway after Gemma Grainger's team won 2-0 in Romania on Friday.

Even if Wales topple the Norwegians, who are ranked 14th in the world, they may then have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a place at next summer's World Cup in Brazil.

99-Year-Old NASCAR Fan Finally Gets Her Dream Ride at Michigan Speedway
description: Shirley Hipple has followed NASCAR for nearly 70 years. As her 100th birthday approaches, the Michigan superfan finally got to experience the thrill of riding in a stock car at Michigan International Speedway.
fullText:
For nearly 70 years, Shirley Hipple experienced NASCAR the same way millions of fans do: from the comfort of her living room, watching the cars race around the track on television.

But at 99 years old, with her 100th birthday approaching, Hipple finally got to experience something she'd spent decades watching from afar.

She climbed into a stock car at Michigan International Speedway and went for a ride.

The experience, arranged through a senior living community's adventure program, gave the longtime NASCAR fan a chance to hear the engines, feel the speed and see the track from a perspective she had only imagined.

And after seven decades of following the sport, it was quite a way to celebrate a milestone birthday.

Hipple's love for racing dates back to the 1950s, when she took her young children to dirt tracks near Groesbeck Highway and Eight Mile Road in Detroit.

What began as family outings developed into a lifelong passion. She followed NASCAR through generations of drivers, championship battles and changes to the sport, rarely missing a race on television.

Her favorite driver became seven-time Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, whose jacket she proudly wore as part of her racing collection.

According to Kinship Company, Hipple even turned her room at Waltonwood Carriage Park in Canton, Michigan, into a tribute to the sport she loved.

But there was one experience she had never checked off her list: actually riding in a stock car.

Through Waltonwood's Adventure program, which helps residents fulfill longtime wishes, Hipple traveled to Michigan International Speedway for a NASCAR ride-along.

Dressed in racing gear and secured inside the car, she experienced the speed and banking of the two-mile oval firsthand.

For someone who had spent nearly 70 years watching NASCAR on television, it was an entirely different way to appreciate the sport.

The ride wasn't the only highlight of Hipple's visit.

She also received a behind-the-scenes tour of pit road, giving her an up-close look at a part of NASCAR that fans typically experience only through television coverage.

The trip was especially meaningful because it connected Hipple's earliest memories of racing in Detroit with one of Michigan's most recognizable motorsports venues.

Sara Bailey, vice president of sales for Waltonwood, said the experience reflected the purpose of the community's Adventure program.

"At Waltonwood, we believe that passions don't fade with age," Bailey said. "Seeing Shirley's lifelong dream come true is what our Adventure program is all about."

Hipple's story is a reminder of something NASCAR fans understand particularly well: A connection to racing can last a lifetime.

Drivers retire, teams change and the cars evolve, but the excitement that first draws someone to the sport can remain remarkably familiar.

For Hipple, that excitement began at local dirt tracks in the 1950s and eventually carried her all the way to Michigan International Speedway.

Now, as she approaches her 100th birthday, she has a new racing memory to add to a collection nearly seven decades in the making.

And this time, she didn't have to watch it on television.

title: DIRU: Dendrite-inspired recurrent units for learning chaotic dynamics
description: We introduce the Dendrite-Inspired Recurrent Unit (DIRU), a novel recurrent neural network architecture that incorporates compartmentalized computation inspired by the hierarchical processing of biological dendrites. Unlike classical recurrent models, which encode temporal dynamics within a single homogeneous hidden state, DIRU implements multiple interacting nonlinear compartments within each recurrent unit, enabling structured internal computation, hierarchical state formation, and adaptive dynamical processing. We evaluate DIRU on canonical chaotic systems, including the Lorenz attractor and the Mackey–Glass time-delay system, using multi-step forecasting tasks that explicitly probe long-horizon stability, error growth consistent with bounded chaotic dynamics, and regime preservation. Across all benchmarks, DIRU demonstrates consistently lower prediction error and more stable training dynamics than baseline models across the evaluated settings, with statistically supported performance differences under controlled capacity conditions. To assess real-world biological relevance, we further evaluate DIRU on neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) seizure classification using the Helsinki Neonatal EEG dataset.

title: Edwards joins Argentina as defence coach
description: Defence coach Shaun Edwards joins Argentina's coaching staff on a deal that runs until the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.
fullText:
Defence coach Shaun Edwards has joined Argentina's coaching staff on a deal that runs until the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The announcement ends any speculation that Edwards could be handed a role in Steve Borthwick's England set-up, with the 59-year-old set to fulfil his consultancy role with England's women's team before joining Felipe Contepomi's staff.

"I'm delighted to join Felipe Contepomi, his coaching staff and the Argentina rugby team at the end of this month until the World Cup next year in Australia," said Edwards.

"I've always admired the ability and quality of Argentine players and I hope to bring some of my international experience to the team during the next year," added the former Wigan rugby league great.

Englishman Edwards, who is one of the most decorated coaches in rugby union, left his position as France men's defence coach earlier this year after helping them win three Six Nations titles.

Edwards and former Argentina head coach and hooker Mario Ledesma, who has been appointed to take charge of the forwards, will start work with the Pumas at the end of October.

Argentina are then set to face Ireland, Italy and France in November in Nations Championship matches.

Three-time semi-finalists Argentina have been drawn in a pool with Fiji, Spain and Canada at the World Cup which takes place between 1 October and 13 November in 2027.

Edwards, who also spent a successful 12 years with Wales and won four English titles and two Champions Cups while on Wasps' staff, said in March that he was interested in coaching in the Rugby Championship, the southern hemisphere tournament contested by South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina.

He turned down a chance to coach his country in 2006, believing that the busier fixture list at Wasps would suit him better as he grieved the death of his brother.

Two years later, he opted to take on a defence role with Wales, rather than lead England's second-string side, then known as the Saxons., external

In 2021, he met with Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney but, without a firm offer forthcoming, signed a contract extension to stay with France.

title: U.S. targets International Criminal Court with new sanctions and an ultimatum
description: The international criminal court (ICC) in The Hague.Photograph: Remko de Waal/ANP/AFP/Getty...
fullText:
The United States was accused of launching "an assault" on the world's legal order after imposing more sanctions on the international criminal court (ICC).

Unveiling the Trump administration's latest escalation against the court, which it has accused of politicization and unfairly targeting Americans for war crime charges, Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, declared: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC."

The ICC accused Donald Trump's officials of attempting to "obstruct the course of justice" as Rubio, just hours after a former ICC judge was awarded the Nobel peace prize, announced in a video that the US would move to impose financial sanctions.

"We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling their ability to operate against us. Because our message is clear: the United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC," Rubio said in a video posted on X. "We don't need that court and we don't want it."

In a statement, the court warned that "history will judge this moment" and urged other members to ensure it can continue the function. "It is an ⁠attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the Court from doing what ⁠it was created to do. It is an assault ​on the rule ‌of law and ‌on the very foundations of the international legal order," ‌the ICC said.

The new set of sanctions will block any assets the ICC has in US jurisdictions and gives US companies or individuals six months to wind down business with the tribunal court.

But the sanctions also allow the ICC to address the US government's concerns, and certain transactions are exempt.

The Trump administration has repeatedly condemned the ICC for issuing arrest warrants for Israeli officials, including Israel's prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. It also opened an investigation into the actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, although the case has been closed.

The ICC was established in 2002 as an international tribunal to hold countries accountable for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity.

Trump has long targeted the ICC. During his first term, he imposed sanctions on the court, which were later reversed under the Biden administration.

But when Trump returned to office in 2025, he signed an executive order imposing sanctions on the ICC for the court's investigations into Israelis and Americans. From there, the administration has continued to impose more sanctions.

The administration added sanctions on judges and lawyers at the ICC. In August, it placed additional sanctions on the ICC president, Tomoko Akane.

title: Greek takeaways: What did we learn from Lionesses' win?
description: England come away from Greece with a valuable first-leg lead in their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off - but who impressed in the 3-1 victory?
fullText:
England came away from Greece with a valuable first-leg lead in their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off - but what did we learn?

Sarina Wiegman's side are looking to secure their place in Brazil next year but have to navigate the play-offs after finishing runners-up in their qualification group.

The back-to-back European champions won 3-1 in Crete on Friday night and will need to finish the job against Greece on Tuesday in Leicester (19:30 BST).

The winner of the tie faces Ukraine or Slovakia in round two to decide who will head to Brazil.

Lucy Bronze withdrew from the squad with a minor injury earlier this week, handing a rare opportunity to Manchester United captain Maya le Tissier.

The defender is a key player for her club but struggles to break into the England team with Bronze understandably a tough figure to displace.

Wiegman sees Le Tissier as a right-back as opposed to a centre-back - which is her position at United - and that meant she was handed a start against Greece.

Making her 15th cap, Le Tissier was a standout performer and was rewarded with her first international goal in the 63rd minute, providing optimism for a future without 34-year-old Bronze.

"As soon as we were in possession, she was higher on the pitch and she already came close to a couple of moments with crosses," said Wiegman.

"I'm very happy for her and for the whole team because that was an important goal."

It was just England's third win in their past eight competitive away games.

A 3-1 victory is a pleasing result, but given the gulf in class, Wiegman admitted frustrations at not keeping a clean sheet.

There were familiar lapses in concentration defensively that gave Greece opportunities to pounce. Ioanna Papatheodorou struck the crossbar in the first half, before teeing up Kallisti Brouksair for their goal later on.

Those chances came from England errors and the lack of clean sheet means the door remains open for Greece in the second leg.

"That's up to us. We have to show up on Tuesday, play a good game and then we should be better than Greece," said Wiegman.

"Of course we want to take some more distance [in the scoreline], that's absolutely true, but at the same time we won and that's the most important thing.

"Sometimes we played really well and sometimes we were a bit sloppy. We were a bit frustrated as we wanted to do that better.

"We want to show more than winning, we want to play really well too."

With victory secure, Wiegman was able to hand a debut to 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson, as well as Liverpool captain Grace Fisk.

Fisk, 28, had waited more than six years for her debut, having received her first England call-up in 2020 but Parkinson has broken through at pace this season.

The teenager was unexpectedly named in Wiegman's squad in March, having only made the jump up to England's Under-23s a few months earlier.

She secured a move to the United States this summer, joining North Carolina Courage from Portuguese side Valadares Gaia, and came on in the 85th minute.

This week defender Esme Morgan said: "She's a really intelligent player. She has incredibly good movement and timing, picking up pockets for players to find her.

"She's really comfortable receiving [the ball] in tight spaces, she's strong holding off players, very aggressive in her tackling and wins back a lot of balls.

"I've been really impressed with Erica since she came into camp and also from playing against her in the National Women's Soccer League."

Why England teenager Parkinson has a mindset coach

Parkinson's debut added to the debate of who Wiegman's preferred number 10 is.

She is one of many options available, including Chelsea forward Lauren James, who was given a creative, free role against Greece.

James showed flashes of quality and nonchalantly lobbed goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti from 30 yards in the first half, but her effort was ruled out for offside.

Other options include Manchester City's Grace Clinton and Manchester United's Ella Toone, who were both recalled to the squad to cover injuries with Aston Villa's Lucia Kendall among those to drop out.

Laura Blindkilde Brown started in that position with James in Crete, while Beth Mead and Jess Park have also played there before.

The position was a difficult one for Wiegman to nail down at Euro 2025 and more than a year later, the question of who is England's best number 10 remains.

"I see there is a lot of competition in that position, where we have a lot of options with different players, who have different qualities," said Wiegman.

"You can call it a question mark but I call it many options. Today we had two 10s and sometimes three. [James] was one of them."

Local media had questioned why the game wasn't being played in Greece's capital city Athens.

And there was an eerie atmosphere with fewer than 4,000 fans in the 26,000-capacity stadium in Heraklion, Crete.

The Lionesses are also not used to being in play-offs, a route they are having to take after finishing runners-up to world champions Spain in their qualifying group.

But Georgia Stanway, this year's top scorer for England, once again turned up when they needed her to and she opened the scoring after a neat, incisive passing move, in a frustrating first half.

That was the spark England needed as they lacked ruthlessness and failed to capitalise on their dominance - an aspect of their game that needs improving.

"I think we made it a bit harder. Greece were well prepared and disciplined. We struggled when they tried to press us," added Wiegman.

"We could have scored more than the three goals. There are lots of things to take. I have seen some fluid moments but I want more.

"The final ball, final cross and the positions can be better. Of course, we are working on that. We have an opportunity to improve that on Tuesday."

title: How Cadillac’s Formula 1 Team Is Struggling to Find Stability and Success
description: The VP of Global Motorsport at General Motors and the team’s top exec talk challenges, potential, and necessary next steps.
fullText:
Eric Warren worked in defense and at NASA prior to his current role as vice president for Global Motorsport Competition at General Motors. Top tier motor racing isn't rocket science; in many ways it's more difficult than that. "I hesitate to say we should have won," he says of Cadillac's performance earlier this year in the 24 Hours of Le Mans (with Hertz Team Jota), "but we certainly could have won, and that's a big step forward."

The truth is, GM has serious form here, more than it gets credit for, with lots more to come. Ford's motorsport-crazy C.E.O. Jim Farley is a passionate, high-profile advocate for the Blue Oval's racing exploits, but GM comfortably eclipses Ford in terms of multidiscipline commitment. WEC, IMSA, NASCAR, IndyCar, the NHRA, off-road truck racing, Australian supercars—GM is highly active in all of it.

First Drive: Bugatti's Bolide Hypercar Is a Meteoric Machine on Miami's F1 Circuit

Tyrese Gibson and Cody Walker on Bringing the 'Fast & Furious' Franchise to Life With Their FuelFest Tour

Lewis Hamilton Bought His Dream Car, the Iconic Ferrari F40

But it's Cadillac's presence in Formula 1 that's indicative of the mothership's ambitions for its increasingly impressive luxury brand. From zero to debuting at the Australian GP earlier this year was no mean feat, and it earned the hat-tip respect of rivals. But for all that F1 is as a globally effective shop window with unparalleled reach among key new demographics, simply showing up is categorically not enough. Cadillac has endured some persistent reliability issues and needs to surmount them.

"We want to compete for wins. We wouldn't be in it if we didn't plan on competing for wins—in every category we're racing in worldwide, not just F1," Warren says firmly. "I've been around some defense industry stuff, NASA is my background, and I've seen a lot of amazing things. But these new F1 engines are incredible. These are tools that are working hard. You're also constantly analyzing data. There's no more data-rich environment than this."

As the F1 season heads onto the home straight, and with both the Austin and Vegas Grands Prix races in prospect, it's a useful time to recap how the U.S. newcomer has been doing. GM's big F1 play, of course, grew out of Andretti Motorsport's bid to become the 11th team in the elite race series. As ever in this intensely political world, various forces had to align, and big names placated, before things could progress. Existing stakeholders had to be mollified so that F1's prize fund could grow to accommodate a new team rather than be diluted. (I recall Christian Horner, former principal for the Red Bull F1 Team, being especially vocal on this matter.)

Dan Towriss, C.E.O. of TWG Motorsports (and now of the Cadillac Formula 1 Team as well), assumed control of the bid, and made the approach. Towriss has the energy and vibe of one of the main characters in Showtime's Billions saga. GM's vice president of Performance and Motorsports, Jim Campbell, remembers meeting him and his wife in a lift on the way to an IndyCar function a few years ago. Had GM thought about F1? "It really was an elevator pitch," Campbell says. Internally, the conversations began in 2022.

"We saw the potential and you could argue we got in on it a little bit late," Warren attests. "But we're still pretty early on the growth cycle. It was a matter of opportunity. It was important that we didn't just sponsor, we want to be a critical part of it, to collaborate fully. We get in and race in all the series we do, although we support teams differently in each. If we come in, we're coming in as partners. Strategy platforms, tools, setups, simulators, aero, CFD . . . everything that it takes to design and build a car, we do."

The opportunity to partner with TWG was key, but so too was the introduction of the cost cap in F1 (initiated in 2021, set at $215 million for 2026). Technical transfer for Cadillac and throughout the wider group is part of the mission, but anyone who has attended an F1 race recently will know that the brand-building possibilities are phenomenal—think Coachella with a motor race attached. The so-called "fan zones" are becoming bigger and more ambitious at every race. "We want to build the Cadillac brand, for the fans. The demographic is changing and getting younger. A lot of things are lining up," Campbell says.

As is the direction of travel on the power-train front. F1's nominal 50-50 internal combustion/electric hybrid format has proven controversial at best and is actively disliked by many of the drivers. The farcical situation that unfolded at last weekend's Bahrain GP–held in Sepang, in Malaysia–has only deepened the malaise: a software bug left Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, and others stranded on the track prior to a system reboot and restart. It was not a good look.

The auto manufacturers who are the commercial mainstays of Formula 1 demand an emphasis on electrification and sustainability. But the requirements for energy management and power-starved engines have compromised pure racing—particularly in terms of overtaking and cornering speeds—throughout the 2026 season. Although, as ever, it depends on who you ask.

Cadillac is currently constructing a power-train manufacturing facility in Concord, N.C, bolstering bases in Silverstone and Indiana, the aim being for the team to have its own engine good-to-go for the 2029 season. (It's currently using Ferrari's power unit.) The proposed return to a V-8 is presumably good news for the all-American team, right?

"We need to work in both directions, the hybrid V-6, the current platform, but also keep an eye on the V-8," says Warren cautiously. "Our statement on this is that we want to support the series. Certainly, we have a lot of products with V-8s in the Americas. It's in the Cadillac hypercar. We do lots of engines, we've raced in a lot of series . . . We like the sound of a [V-8], a lot of the elements, get some cost out of it . . . there's a lot of positives, but I think it's about trying to support the series. We want something that's exciting for the fans and the competitors, and for the series."

Is it imperative that Cadillac runs an American driver? Warren plays it down. Finding the home-grown equivalent of Mercedes-AMG's break-out superstar Kimi Antonelli is desirable but not essential. "We want to be authentically American, certainly regarding ownership and everything. But we want to race competitively. There's a pathway to get to that, but just putting an American in there when the car's not ready or the team's not ready, just to say it's American, no. We want to continue progressing and we knew it was going to be hard," Warren continues. "It's difficult for me to say that we're happy, because every week you want to see progression. We're proud of what it's taken to get here. But there's a difference being proud and being happy . . . that's the long-term goal. We won't be happy until we compete for wins."

It also seems that patience in getting to that point is decidedly finite. Robb Report spoke to Graeme Lowdon, Cadillac's team principal, during the Hungarian GP earlier this year. A well-liked figure in the paddock, Lowdon was instrumental in realizing Cadillac's F1 dream from a blank sheet of paper. Personnel, infrastructure, design, engineering, coffee machines—the lot.

"We're not just here to make up the numbers. We have a bold ambition to build a substantial and successful team, but it does take some time," Lowden explained when we spoke. "I was talking to another team principal, discussing a particularly successful stage at one team. 'Yeah, you know the reason for that success was the six years of failure beforehand,' he reminded me. People forget just how long it takes to get there. But this is a sport where it's maximum attack all the time on every front. The common denominator in sustained success is stability."

Note the past tense in describing Lowdon's role. When I mentioned to Lowdon that figures like Dan Towriss aren't generally known for being patient, he forced a smile. It's likely to have been the last interview he did as Cadillac's team principal. Despite his insistence on stability, Towriss evidently disagreed. Lowdon was fired shortly after we spoke, and had no inkling it was coming.

"It wasn't a mutual decision," Towriss explained in a media call shortly after. "The process started a few months ago: really thinking about what the next phase for Cadillac Formula 1, what's the right timing, how would that look, and then the capabilities of the various folks out there."

Cadillac F1's new team principal is ex-Alpine F1 executive director Marcin Budkowski. With the team up and running, improving on-track competitiveness is now critical. As we head into this weekend's Singapore GP, the team has come tantalizingly close but has yet to score any championship points. One of its drivers, Valtteri Bottas, elected to ride a bicycle from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore rather than fly. It's a distance of around 220 miles, which should give him time to think.

"There's no easy way to make this transition within Formula 1 . . . It does compress the decision-making, the timeline, and how these things come together," Towriss admits. "It makes it feel more abrupt than it would otherwise be. But it's the nature of Formula 1 and it's the way it had to happen." Formula 1 is famously known as the "piranha club." Results are all that matter. And while Cadillac has arrived, it must now prove as hungry and aggressive as the others.

Major League Baseball has announced the television schedule for the 2026 League Championship Series.

The action begins on Oct. 11 in an NLCS showdown the baseball world has figured would happen for months, and it's a rematch of last year's NLCS. The two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers go on the road to face Jacob Misiorowski and the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 (8 p.m.). Joe Davis and John Smoltz will have the NLCS television call for Fox Sports.

title: Sam Altman says AI will make ‘bad things’ happen. Exhibit A: needless death | Moustafa Bayoumi
description:
AI is already implicated in violent deaths and nearly started world war three. Those bad things? They only happen to other people
Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, has some words for you about his company and the future of artificial intelligence.
“One of the differences between us and some of the stricter AI safety people is that we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency [to use it],” Altman told Politico’s new technology podcast and newsletter Decoded.
Moustafa Bayoumi is the author of the award-winning books How Does It Feel to Be a Problem?
fullText:
AI is already implicated in violent deaths and nearly started world war three. Those bad things? They only happen to other people

Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, has some words for you about his company and the future of artificial intelligence.

“One of the differences between us and some of the stricter AI safety people is that we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency [to use it],” Altman told Politico’s new technology podcast and newsletter Decoded.

Yikes. This statement – and the approach it represents – is, well, problematic, to say the least. It’s also emblematic of precisely the kind of world-building and world-destroying that is happening with today’s technology in front of all our eyes, with precious little input from the rest of us.

Altman’s mention of the “bad things” that AI might bring makes it sound like AI’s failures mistakenly create innocent, minor problems or even silly little episodes, such as the time when Google’s “AI Overviews” told users to put non-toxic glue on pizza so the cheese will be less likely to slide off. Good advice is helpful. Bad advice? Chalk it up to being a bad thing.

But culinary adventurism is hardly the only realm that AI operates in and the damage AI is inflicting has already and repeatedly proven itself to be dangerous and even potentially deadly to humans.

OpenAI is embroiled in a lawsuit after the tragic suicide of Adam Raine, a 16-year-old student who initially began using OpenAI’s ChatGPT for homework help. The family’s lawsuit alleges that the teenager took his own life with the chatbot’s encouragement. (OpenAI has claimed Raine misused the platform.)

And Raine’s action is hardly the only one. OpenAI is facing multiple lawsuits filed by different families of victims of suicide and self-harm.

Nor is suicide the only “bad thing” to emerge in the AI universe. In February of this year, on the first day of the war in Iran, two Tomahawk missiles struck the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in the city of Minab, killing at least 120 children. (A UN fact-finding mission concluded that the US was probably responsible for the strike.)

In a recent investigation into the attack, Bloomberg News reported that an AI-linked system was used to target the school. In this case, the system is called Maven, and it is made by Palantir.

Unnamed defense officials told Bloomberg that “inside Centcom, which conducted the US attack, some personnel relied too much on the artificial intelligence embedded in Maven Smart System”. The report also adds that “in the past year, the Defense Department has rapidly made Maven a cornerstone of the US military apparatus”.

AI is helping to produce these tragic and needless deaths, but bad things happen, I guess.

Or there’s the little detail that the US may have come within a hair’s breadth of starting a major war against a superpower, all due to an AI error.

In September, CNN reported that an unidentified AI chatbot used by the US military decided that a Chinese ship in Middle Eastern waters was carrying components of a nuclear weapons program. According to CNN, US planes took off on an interception mission and US military personnel were preparing to board the ship.

Only then did the military look more closely at the report they were basing the mission on and realize the chatbot’s mistakes.

Also found in CNN’s frightening story is that the analyst who used the chatbot to come up with the shoddy analysis then used AI again to write the report, which set the whole thing in motion. A twofer of bad things, I suppose.

Why does it seem that these technologies, which, in the words of Trump’s White House, are “empowering Americans to achieve what was previously impossible across science, medicine, and nearly every other domain of human endeavor”, get such serious stuff so wrong and so often?

And isn’t it true that the more we rely on AI, the more dangerous these little mistakes become? And why were we never consulted about any of this in the first place?

Could it be that what’s behind the artificial intelligence revolution may be less about the utopian or dystopian future (take your pick) that’s just around the corner and more about the enormous amount of money that is being poured into these companies in the present?

AI may be the only thing keeping Trump’s economy afloat right now. And it’s paying dividends. According to the New Yorker, OpenAI “is reportedly preparing for an initial public offering at a potential valuation of a trillion dollars” and Sam Altman “may become one of the wealthiest and most powerful people on the planet”.

Those bad things? They only happen to other people.

Meanwhile, we are being warned almost every day that AI systems are getting so smart that they’ll end humanity.

But maybe the real worry here is not that the machines are taking over.

It’s that the humans are giving up, ceding control and responsibility in the name of hyping up a product that has shown itself as being really good at taking jobs away from people, stealing the intellectual property of others, writing some piss-poor undergraduate essays, spying on you and your license plates and bringing us to the brink of world war three because God forbid humans should actually question the output from machines. Or the makers of those machines.

What we need is real, tangible and enforceable government oversight over these technologies, which are quickly becoming a dominating force in all our lives. We must collectively have the right to decide how AI should be used. And despite what you may hear, China already regulates its AI companies quite aggressively.

Instead, Donald Trump, Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta and Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia believe that the AI companies should simply regulate themselves, so they have come up with something called the AI Accords.

Signed by leaders of Meta, Nvidia, Google, Anthropic, xAI and OpenAI, the accords ask tech companies to “implement robust internal controls and monitor the capabilities and alignment of its models”, among other things. “Over time,” the agreement states, “it may make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations.”

Trump, who has ordered the term artificial intelligence be discarded for “super intelligence”, posted the accord on social media on 29 September. The document, titled The White House Accord on Super Intelligence, can still be seen on his account and the White House’s official account. It’s signed by all six tech leaders and Trump, who in the document is labeled “President of the Unites States.”
